title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Per-Customer Allotment on a Sailing
content:
## Clause

Each sailing offers every shipper only a limited allotment of hazardous cargo under Dangerous Goods Acceptance, so the line adds acceptances up per customer and per sailing. When a new application or an amendment is handled, the containers it would put on its acceptance are added to the containers the same customer already has counted on that sailing for the same category. That total may not go above the category's per-customer maximum for one sailing. An application or amendment whose total would go above it is refused for that sailing; the shipper may instead apply on another booking whose sailing still has room.

## What goes into the count already on the sailing

- **Whose containers:** those of the customer that is the applicant.
- **Which sailing:** the vessel voyage the booking concerned is allocated to, taken from the booking record; every booking of that customer allocated to the same vessel voyage contributes.
- **Which acceptances:** those of the same category, standing on the handling date as submitted, under review or approved.
- **Never counted:** rejected acceptances and withdrawn acceptances, and the acceptance being handled itself.
- **Authority:** the line's own acceptance and booking records, consulted at the time of handling; a figure offered by the customer does not replace them.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** containers of the application or the amended declaration; containers already counted as above; the category's per-customer sailing maximum.
- **Judgement:** does the first figure, together with the second, exceed the third?
- **Output:** if it does not, the allotment holds; if it does, the application or amendment is refused on that sailing.

## Hypothetical boundary cases

The figures below are invented for illustration and are not tariff values. Suppose a maximum of 9 containers and 6 already counted: an application for 3 containers brings the total to exactly 9 and stays within the allotment, while one for 4 brings it to 10 and is refused on that sailing. A rejected acceptance of 5 containers on the same voyage would change neither outcome, since it is outside the count.
